producer_report.summary:
Drain now rebuilds and re-executes Athena after landing a change to its own code, and a stale-build line is printed in the places the request named.

**Rebuild and re-exec (`drain.rs`, `main.rs`, `wiring.rs`)**
- `Steps::rebuild` is a new injectable step. After a landing that touches `crates/`, `xtask/`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `setup.sh`, it runs once, before the next job starts. Landings wait while it builds.
- The real step (`run_setup`) runs `sh setup.sh` in the checkout, so there is no second copy of the build steps. A checkout with no `setup.sh` builds nothing.
- On success the pass ends as the new stop reason `rebuilt`. `Report::restart` holds the remaining budget and job limit, plus the same rating threshold.
- `follow_restart` hands those to the restart call. In `main.rs` that replaces the process with `$ATHENA_HOME/bin/athena drain --budget <left> --rating-threshold <n> --job-limit <left> [--json]`.
- The installed path is used, not `current_exe`, because the running file has been replaced on disk.
- A stop asked for with `drain-stop` wins over the restart. A run with no job limit or budget left ends as `job limit` or `budget spent` instead.
- On failure the run stops as `rebuild failed`, and `Report::rebuild_output` holds the exit status and script output. `display::drain` prints it.
- The rebuild failure replaces any other stop reason found at the same time. No rating is taken, and the landing stands.

**Stale-build line (`status.rs`, `display.rs`, `main.rs`)**
- `stale_build_line` runs `git diff --name-only <build> HEAD -- <paths>` when the build commit is an ancestor of HEAD. It gives no line for a build that names no commit, a commit this repository lacks, or only `docs/` or `records/` changes.
- `athena status` prints the line and carries it as `stale_build` in the JSON. `go`, `drain`, `audit` and `audience` print the same line to standard error through one helper, `warn_if_stale`.

**Docs**
- `CHANGELOG.md` has two entries. `docs/decisions.md` has a new D140. I also added the two new stop reasons to the `drain` help text.

**Tests**
- New tests in `crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs` cover:
  - one rebuild, with the second item running under the new build;
  - a failed rebuild stopping the drain with the build output;
  - docs-only landings rebuilding nothing;
  - the job-limit and stop-requested cases;
  - the re-exec arguments;
  - the path rules;
  - the real `setup.sh` runner;
  - the status line with and without a `crates/` change.
- Targeted runs pass: the drain, binary and version test files, and the athena-cli unit tests. Clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
- I ran the full `cargo test --locked` once. The tool returned without an error, but its output was saved to a path I can't read here, so I could not confirm the pass counts myself.

cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain --test binary --test version
checks_run.note: 94 drain, 15 binary and 4 version tests passed

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: a test drains two fake items where the first landing changes a crates/ file; it shows the rebuild step ran exactly once and the second item ran under the new build commit.
criteria_check.evidence: `a_landing_that_changes_athenas_code_rebuilds_once_and_the_next_item_runs_under_the_new_build` in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs. It drains items a and b, where a's landing changes a crates/ file. It asserts the stop is `Rebuilt`, the remaining limits are 9 jobs and $8.20, the stub log has exactly one "rebuild" entry, and the runs were [(a, old), (b, new)] after `follow_restart`. I ran it: `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain -- rebuild` passed.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: a test shows a failed rebuild stops the drain with stop reason 'rebuild failed' and includes the build output.
criteria_check.evidence: `a_failed_rebuild_stops_the_drain_as_rebuild_failed_with_the_build_output` asserts `Stop::RebuildFailed`, label "rebuild failed", `rebuild_output` equal to the fake build text, no restart, no second item run, no rating taken, and that `display::drain` shows "stopped     rebuild failed" and the output. `the_real_rebuild_runs_the_checkouts_setup_script_and_reports_its_output_when_it_fails` shows the real runner returns the exit status and the script's stdout and stderr. Both passed when I ran them.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: a test shows status prints the stale-build line when a crates/ file changed after the build commit, and prints none when only docs/ or records/ changed.
criteria_check.evidence: `status_prints_the_stale_build_line_after_a_crates_change_and_none_after_docs_or_records_changes` uses a real git fixture. Built from HEAD, there is no line. After a commit that adds docs/notes.md and records/notes.md, there is still no line. After a crates/ commit, `display::status` prints exactly one "stale build" line naming both short commits. The xtask, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and setup.sh paths also trigger it, and a build commit of "unknown" gives none. It passed when I ran it.

criteria_check.criterion: go, drain, audit and audience print the same one-line stale-build warning when the build commit is older than HEAD for the watched paths.
criteria_check.evidence: In main.rs, `Command::Go`, `Command::Drain`, `Command::Audit` and `Command::Audience` each call `warn_if_stale(&athena)` right after `open(true)`. It prints `Athena::stale_build()` to standard error, the same `stale_build_line` that `athena status` prints. There is no binary-level test, because a cargo test build names no commit. The line's condition is covered by the status test and `athena.stale_build()` assertions.

criteria_check.criterion: The re-exec passes the remaining budget and job limit.
criteria_check.evidence: `Restart` carries the unspent budget and the job limit minus jobs started (asserted 9 and 8.2 in the rebuild test). `follow_restart` passes `Restart::limits()` to the restart call, and `main.rs` runs `reexec(&drain::reexec_args(&left, json))`. `the_new_binary_is_started_with_the_remaining_budget_and_job_limit` asserts the args [drain, --budget, 8.25, --rating-threshold, 3, --job-limit, 9]. The re-exec uses the installed binary and `CommandExt::exec`; only the argument list and the hand-off are tested, not an actual exec.

criteria_check.criterion: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy with -D warnings and cargo test all pass.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. I ran `cargo fmt --all --check` (clean), `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` (clean), and `cargo test --locked` once (returned without an error; output unread).

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the self-rebuild and stale-build warning.
criteria_check.evidence: CHANGELOG.md, under Unreleased > Added, has two new entries: the drain self-rebuild and re-exec with `rebuilt` and `rebuild failed`, and the stale-build line in `status` and the go, drain, audit and audience commands.

open_issues: A restarted drain forgets its earlier landings, so a "target met" in the new process needs a landing in that process. This is recorded as a tradeoff in D140.
The first pass's final report is not printed; its progress lines already went to standard error.
If the checkout has uncommitted changes, setup refuses a non-dirty build. The rebuild then fails and the drain stops with `rebuild failed` and the script output. I did not pass --allow-dirty.
The four commands' stale-build warning has no binary-level test, because a cargo test build names no commit.
mistakes: I read very large files in full (drain.rs, status.rs) early on, which used a lot of budget; I should have used Grep for the relevant sections.
I did not unit-test the actual `exec` call, since it would replace the test process; only the arguments and the hand-off are tested.
learnings: The build commit comes from ATHENA_BUILD_COMMIT, set by `xtask build_and_adopt` (the setup step); it is embedded through `wiring::build_info()`. The binary is installed at $ATHENA_HOME/bin/athena. A cargo test build names no commit, so it reports "unknown".
A landing fast-forwards the local checkout (commits.rs), so running setup.sh in `athena.git.dir()` builds from the landed tree.
`RealSteps` is built with a struct literal in about 25 tests, so new behavior had to go on the `Steps` trait with a default method and not on new `RealSteps` fields.
`drain_help_documents_the_flags_and_lists_every_stop_reason` requires every `Stop::ALL` label to appear in the drain help text.
The Bash tool here allows only cargo, git, ls, chmod, mv and rm. The Grep and Read tools cannot read the persisted tool-output files outside the working directory.
desires: A way to read saved tool output files, or a quieter full-suite mode, so the suite result can be confirmed without rerunning it.
A runtime override of the build commit (an environment variable) so the go, drain, audit and audience warnings could be exercised through the real binary.
